name: What is the real all-in cost per square foot for a custom home in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: What does all-in custom home cost per square foot include in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What does all-in custom home cost per square foot include in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: A useful Los Angeles custom-home budget should distinguish construction-only pricing from true all-in cost. Construction-only numbers often exclude architecture, structural engineering, permits, utility work, landscaping, and contingency. In expensive neighborhoods and on complex sites, soft costs can materially increase the total budget. That is why two homes with similar square footage can land in very different budget ranges. The best way to compare builders is to ask for a line-item estimate that shows hard costs, soft costs, and allowances separately. That lets homeowners see whether a quote is realistic or artificially low. It also helps prevent budget surprises after design decisions, permit conditions, or site discoveries change the scope.
acceptedAnswer.description: All-in cost per square foot should include design, engineering, permits, site work, construction, finishes, and contingency, not just the build itself. In Los Angeles, that all-in number is often far higher than construction-only pricing, especially when soft costs and site complexity are included.
